q1_issues.issue: The kind-level relation form is used although 'the oppressor' and 'the oppressed' are definite singulars, which the instruction set explicitly excludes from that trigger (both arguments must be bare kind-denoting NPs), so this clause should have reified an event or a distributing rule instead of (Defeat power oppressor) / (Defeat power oppressed).

The reduced relative 'wrongly used' is emitted as a free-standing asserted use event with no link to the main predication, so the parse asserts both that power is wrongly used and that power defeats unconditionally, losing the sentence's restriction of the claim to wrongly-used power.

q2_gaps: a restrictive participial modifier that restricts a generic / kind-level claim ('power, wrongly used, defeats X'): participial post-modifiers are reified as asserted events and generics become rules, but nothing says how to make the main claim conditional on the modifier
a verbal generic whose subject is a bare mass / abstract noun ('power'), which supplies no instance range for the Implication rule form
'as well as' as a coordinator; the instruction set names 'as well' only as an additive focus particle (Also), and the coordination section covers only 'X and Y'
notes: Defeat itself is a licensed head shape under the open-class kind-relation license, so the defect is the routing, not the vocabulary. Theme for the object of 'use' and the surface-form Manner adverb 'wrongly' both follow the instruction set.
